šuššum: one-sixth (written IGI.6.GAL, “the sixth part”): šuššum “a sixth”; in the silver rate it is followed by 6 še, “one-sixth and 6 grains” (IGI.6.GAL šeššet šeʾam)
6: six — six vertical wedges (6): šeššet “six” before šeʾum, where the 6 counts the barleycorns (še) that make up the fraction of a shekel
nakārum: UNCERTAIN: perhaps nakārum “to be hostile, to deny, to dispute”: only the first sign ik survives, which the editor doubts, so the form (ikkir-ma ?) and the sense are a guess; the verb is the editors’ restoration
watārum-D: D-stem of watārum, to make exceed, increase: uwatte… (broken; uwattir / uwattar “he increases”, with -ma “and”); the interest raised above the rate
ulu: or (u-lu, a conjunction, “or … or”): ulu … ulu “either … or”, “or … or”, linking the clauses of a list
ḫerûm-Š: UNCERTAIN: the verb ḫerûm “to dig, to scratch”; here a Š-stem perfect, uštaḫri… (uš-ta-aḫ-ri-[šu]-ma, broken), “he had (it) dug / scratched out”; both the reading and the sense (a debt struck from its tablet) are guesses
eliûm: upper, higher: ṭuppam eliam “an upper tablet” (accusative, written e-li-am); the editors understand a supplementary tablet, which is uncertain
qaqqadum: head; the capital, the principal of a loan, as against its interest (written SAG.DU, “head”): ana qaqqadim “to the capital” (genitive, written with the logogram)
tēḫûm-D: UNCERTAIN: D-stem of the verb teḫûm “to approach”: “to bring near, add to”; uttēḫḫi “he added (it)” (a D perfect) in ṣibātim ana qaqqadim uttēḫḫi “he added the interest to the capital”; the form and the sense are partly a guess, and the verb is distinct from the noun tēḫûm of gap-a
šanûm-Š: UNCERTAIN: šanûm “to repeat, do a second time”, so perhaps “to double”; uštašannâ (uš-ta-ša-an-na-ma, with -ma “and”) is a Š-stem perfect (ušta- is the perfect prefix) and is read as “he shall double (it)”, but the exact stem and the form are not secure; the sense follows the penalty of the law
maṭûm: to be small, short, few; maṭītim (feminine, genitive) “small”, said of a measure: ina GIŠ.BAR maṭītim “by a small measure”; in the first occurrence (§95, line 4) the ma and ṭi are doubtful signs
GIŠ.BAR: UNCERTAIN: a Sumerogram (GIŠ + BAR) whose Akkadian reading I do not know; the context suggests a measure (of grain), with the adjective “small”; kept as written and not read aloud
NER: UNCERTAIN: the sign KIŠ read ner (Harper’s sign list); the word is not known to me and the editors call it a “control”; kept as written, with no gloss
upaṣ: UNCERTAIN: a verb of the merchant in the law of the borrower’s goods: u-pa-aṣ after ul “not”; its meaning is not established from the grammar, and the Assyrian copy’s up-pa-aš-ma may or may not be the same word; left as written and untranslated
tappûtum: partnership: ana tappûtim “for a partnership” (genitive); the word is the editors’ normalized print, and the syllabic spelling tap-pu-tim stands in as a placeholder, uncertain
butuqqûm: loss, claim for loss: butuqqâm (accusative, bu-tu-uq-qa-am, the sign IG read uq)
šamallûm: UNCERTAIN: the merchant’s agent, his trading assistant: šamallim (genitive, ša-ma-al-li-im), šamallû (nominative, ša-ma-al-lu-u₂); the editors print a logogram with a complement, so the syllabic spellings are a placeholder
pašārum: UNCERTAIN: the verb pašārum “to loosen, release”; in the merchant’s law, perhaps “to sell off, dispose of” (ana pašārim, restored by the editors as “for selling”): only pa-ša… survives, so the form and sense are a guess

__broaden__.-šu: his / him · -šum “to him, for him” (dative): išakkanūšum, innadnušum · after a dental the suffix is assimilated and spelled with z: …ssu (ṣibat-zu, ṣibassu “its interest”, written after a broken sign); with a noun: ṣibtišu “its interest”, qātīšu “his hand”, damqaršu “his merchant”; tu-šu, te-šu in broken forms
__broaden__.tamkārum: merchant (written tam-KAR §32, DAM.GÀR §40): the ransom-fronting, land-buying businessman of the code · written dam-qar, dam-qar-um (the common syllabic spelling of the merchant): damqar, damqarum “the merchant” (nominative), damqaršu “his merchant”
__broaden__.kaspum: silver — the code’s money, written KÙ.BABBAR “shining precious-metal” · kaspim: mišil mana kaspim “half a mina of silver” · with a spelled vowel after the logogram: KÙ.BABBAR-a-am, -i-im, -u-um: kaspam, kaspim, kaspum (accusative, genitive, nominative); kaspum as the subject; the grain-and-silver pair šeʾam u kaspam “grain and silver”
__broaden__.ḫubullum: debt, an interest-bearing loan: ḫubullum; bēl ḫubullim “the creditor” · ḫubullam, ḫubullim, written ḫu-bu-ul-lam / ḫu-bu-ul-li-im, and also ḪAR.RA (perhaps the same word, taken so from context, UNCERTAIN): ana ḫubullim “as a loan”, ša ḫubullam ilqû “who took a loan”
__broaden__.nadānum: to give, pay: inaddin, iddinam, iddinušum; nadānim “to give” · iddin “he gave”; ana kaspim nadānum “to sell”: inaddinūma (present, plural) “they shall sell, and …” · iddin, iddinu “he gave” (preterite; the subjunctive -u in a ša- or inūma clause); iddinma “he gave, and”; …in, …din in broken forms; inaddin “he shall give”: ana damqaršu inaddin “he shall give to his merchant”
__broaden__.kurrum: the kor, a grain measure (written GUR; Harper: 300 KA): kur šeʾam “a kor of grain” · written GUR.É (the editors’ print GUR-É) as well as GUR: 1 GUR.É, kurrum “a kor” (UNCERTAIN: the .É is not explained here)
__broaden__.šeʾum: barley, grain (the ŠE sign) · ŠE-am, ŠE-im, ŠE-um, written with the logogram and a spelled vowel; šeʾum as the subject; ŠE-am-ma “grain only” (with the restricting -ma); in broken forms še…
__broaden__.ṣibtum: interest (“increase”): ṣibtam; ṣibassu, ṣibtišu “its interest” · also written MÁŠ (the logogram, “increase”) and ṣib-tam; plural ṣibātim (ṣi-ba-tim) “interest(s)”; ṣibtim genitive
__broaden__.leqûm: to take: ileqqi “he shall take” · ilqi “he took” (il-qi₂), ilqû (subjunctive, il-qu₂-u₂), ilqēma (il-qi₂-e-ma) “he took, and”, ilteqēma (perfect, il-te-qi₂-ma) “he has taken, and”; ša … ilqû “which he took”
__broaden__.târum-D: D-stem of târum: to give back: turru “taken away/captured”; utarrūšumma “they shall return (it) to him” · utâr (present) “he shall hand back” · turrim (infinitive, tu-ur-ri-im): ana turrim “for repaying, to give back”; utâr (present) “he shall hand back”
__broaden__.išûm: to have: lā īšu “he has not” · īšu “he has”, īšû (the subjunctive form, in a clause that continues): ana turrim lā īšû “has not to repay”
__broaden__.kīma: like, as · as, like; with a verb in the subjunctive: kīma ubbalu “as he brings (it)” · according to: kīma ṣimdat šarrim “according to the king’s schedule”
__broaden__.bašûm: to exist, arise: ibbaššû “which arose” · lā ibaššišum “there is not to him” (= he has none), with dative -šum · in broken forms …ši (ul ibašši, “there is not”, the verb itself restored); ibaššû “which are (there)”, in mimma ina qātīšu ibaššû
__broaden__.maḫārum: to receive: imḫur(u) · imḫur, imḫuru “he received” (preterite; subjunctive in a clause), imaḫḫar “he shall receive” (present); …ḫari… in a broken form · to face, withstand (litany): qabal lā maḫārim “combat none can face”
__broaden__.ilum: god; here: the temple as owner · plural ilāni “gods” (written DINGIR.DINGIR, as in the litany): maḫar ilāni “before the gods”
__broaden__.ḫarrānum: road; campaign: ḫarrān šarrim “the king’s campaign” (spelled ḫar-ra-an, or carved with the road-sign KASKAL) · journey, the merchant’s trading trip: ana ḫarrānim “on a journey” (the editors print ḫarranim; the spelling ḫar-ra-nim is uncertain here), ina ḫarrānim “on the journey”
__broaden__.ṭarādum: to send (off): iddarad “he sent (as his substitute)” — Harper’s reading of iṭṭarad · to send: iṭrussu “he sent him” (iṭrud + -šu, the d assimilating: it-ru-uz-zu)
__broaden__.eṣēpum: to arrange duly; muštēṣbi “who arranges in order” · UNCERTAIN: uṣṣap (uṣ-ṣa-ap, the last sign doubtful), a form I cannot place; taken with doubt as “he adds”, from a root ṣ-p; the link with eṣēpum is a guess, and it does not fit “arrange”
__broaden__.alākum: to go: illak “he shall go” · illiku “(where) he went” (preterite, subjunctive -u, after a restored ašar), in the agent law
__broaden__.amārum: to see, examine: immarūma “they shall examine” · ītamar “he has seen” (perfect, singular)
__broaden__.ūmum: day; ūmišu “daily” (written UD-mi-šu) · plural “days”: ūmī (written UD-mi-) “days”: ina ūmīšu lā malûtim “in his days not full” (the days of a lease) · ūm “day” (UD), before a following word, in ūm NER lā “a day (when ?) NER not …”
__broaden__.elûm: to go up; here: to forfeit: ina kaspišu ītelli “he goes up out of his silver” — his money is gone · to come up: īteliānim (perfect, feminine plural, with the ventive -nim) “(the sheep) have come up” · to go up; D-stem ullûm — mulli “who raises high” (litany) · ītelli “he forfeits” (ina mimma ša iddinu ītelli “he forfeits whatever he gave”); ī…, …li in broken forms of the same formula
